summary:
WE build a game based on the challange'The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer'.IT is a bilingual space survival simulator for kids ages 7 to 12.

Space science can easily feel dry and inaccessible to children. To fix this, we gamified real NASA open data—like radiation metrics and communication delays—turning them into core survival mechanics. Players are challenged to survive a 7-day mission on a space outpost by managing power for life support, reacting to sudden solar flares, and completing 3D tasks like drilling for water-ice.

Instead of passively reading about STEM concepts, kids experience them firsthand. By forcing players to navigate strict resource limits and make difficult trade-offs, the game teaches the "butterfly effect" of their decisions. It builds practical critical thinking skills and gives them a genuine appreciation for the harsh realities of actual space exploration.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive English-Chinese bilingual space survival game for children aged 7–12. Players act as commanders at a Lunar South Pole or Mars Jezero Crater base, managing life support, battery power, and solar flares over a 7-day mission.

Instead of rote memorization, kids learn real space science through cause-and-effect gameplay. They balance power across oxygen, shields, and crops, while playing fast-paced mini-games to drill water ice, dodge meteorites, and patch air leaks in 8 seconds. Built on real NASA data (DONKI and OSDR), dropping any resource below 40% triggers realistic domino penalties—like hypoxia slowing movement or 14-minute Mars radio delays forcing day-ahead planning. At Day 7, a personalized Butterfly Effect Log helps kids review their decisions.

Designed for accessibility with three difficulty levels and seamless bilingual switching for multilingual communities like Sarawak, Malaysia, this lightweight web app runs smoothly in any browser using HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript. Our team independently designed all game mechanics, balancing, and NASA data integration, using Google Gemini to assist with frontend code, data interpretation, and bilingual copyediting.
